title: Temporary structured encampment and 2023 year-end finances
subtitle: Tiny homes proposal, parking penalties, ambulance pre-orders, reserve surplus allocations and new reserve funds also came before the committee.
overview: The committee spent most of the afternoon on the mayoral direction about a temporary structured encampment. Staff recommended taking no further action beyond sending the report to the County of Wellington's new Joint Social Services and Land Ambulance Committee, because the county, as service manager, favours permanent supportive housing. The committee received the report and forwarded it {{vote:m6}}. It then recommended that staff look at municipally owned sites and, with county staff, assess a community tiny homes proposal, reporting back by July 2024 {{vote:m9}}. It also asked the county for an alternative plan and a winter plan if the proposal is not viable {{vote:m11}}. Staff said this work will displace other projects.

Earlier, the committee dealt with 2023 year-end finances. It recommended the capital budget adjustments and early ordering of seven ambulances {{vote:m2}}. It recommended directing the operating surplus mostly to reserves {{vote:m3}}, and new and renamed reserve funds {{vote:m4}}. On consent, it recommended taking over certain provincial offences prosecutions and moving to an administrative penalty system for parking {{vote:m1}}.

These are recommendations. Council must adopt them before they take effect. After the closed session, the chair reported that the committee received information on site safety and security and gave no direction.

decisions.item: Tiny homes proposal and municipal sites
decisions.detail: The committee recommended that staff identify suitable municipally owned sites and costs, that the county be asked to work with staff on assessing the Guelph Tiny Homes Coalition proposal, and that staff report back by July 2024.

The committee recommended asking the county to provide an alternative accessible solution and a winter plan if the tiny homes proposal is not viable, reporting to the Joint Social Services and Land Ambulance Committee.
The committee received the staff report on a temporary structured encampment and directed that it be forwarded to the Joint Social Services and Land Ambulance Committee for information.
The committee recommended that Council authorize agreements to take over certain Provincial Offences Act prosecutions and direct staff to implement an Administrative Penalty System for parking.
The committee recommended approving year-end capital adjustments and early ordering of seven replacement ambulances for a total commitment of $1,768,600 over two years.

The committee recommended allocating the $3,863,029 tax-supported surplus and the $3,414,200 non-tax-supported surplus to or from reserves, including $3,703,389 to the Tax Rate Operating Contingency Reserve and funding the parking and courts deficits from reserves.

The committee recommended opening a Tree Compensation reserve fund, establishing a reserve fund for Property Assessed Clean Energy grant funding, renaming another as the PACE Loan Loss Provision reserve fund, and moving $500 thousand from the stormwater contingency reserve to the stormwater capital reserve fund.

debate: Staff and the CAO said the county, as service manager, holds the expertise, funding role and the by-name list of people seeking housing, and favours permanent supportive housing over temporary encampments. They argued the county must be at the table and that the new joint committee is the place for that discussion.

Delegates urged action before winter. They said some people avoid shelters because of couples, pets, belongings or accessibility needs, and that a tiny homes pilot could serve as a step toward permanent housing. The coalition said it needs a formal endorsement and a site before it will start fundraising.

Councillors questioned the exit strategy and what 'temporary' means. They also raised operating costs, the capacity of stretched service providers, and the gap between staff and coalition operating cost estimates. One councillor said the city's budget limits make longer-term obligations a concern.

Staff said they have no social services department and that the work would displace other projects, such as housing accelerator fund items. Councillors changed the wording to 'request' the county's involvement because the city cannot direct county staff.

On finances, councillors asked whether to pause stormwater fee increases and whether to put money into the affordable housing reserve. Staff advised first rebuilding contingency reserves toward the 75 per cent minimum of target, and said the surplus does not prevent later rate changes.
